question.worked_solution:
We need to express the summation $S(k+1)$ in terms of $S(k).$

Let ${a}_{i}$ for $i\ge 2$ be a sequence, and let $S(k)$ denote the sum of the first $k-1$ terms.

$$
S(k)={\sum }_{i=2}^{k}{a}_{i}
$$

We can always express $S(k+1)$ in terms of $S(k)$ by writing the last term on its own, as follows: 

$$
{\sum }_{i=2}^{k+1}{a}_{i}=({\sum }_{i=2}^{k}{a}_{i})+{a}_{k+1}.
$$

In our case, we have ${a}_{i}=i(i-1).$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{k+1}=(k+1)(k+1-1)=k(k+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
{\sum }_{i=2}^{k+1}i(i-1)=({\sum }_{i=2}^{k}i(i-1))+(k(k+1)),
$$

which we can write as 

$$
S(k+1)=S(k)+k(k+1).
$$
